Only one of the review papers, the 2022 *Advanced Energy Materials* review on cobalt-free cathodes (aenm-2022), cites literature on disordered rock-salt (DRX) cathodes. It cites **11 distinct DRX references: refs. [34]–[44]**.

These appear in the DRX section and its figure captions (Section 5, Figures 8 and 9; aenm-2022, pp. 9–11). The full entries are in the reference list (aenm-2022, p. 15):

| Ref. | Work | What it is cited for |
|---|---|---|
| [34] | Clément, Lun, Ceder, *Energy Environ. Sci.* 2020 | Fade mechanisms, d⁰ cations, isotropic volume change, fluorination, Fig. 8c (cited several times) |
| [35] | Lee et al., *Science* 2014 | Percolating 0-TM Li⁺ diffusion channels, Fig. 8b |
| [36] | Lee et al., *Nature* 2018 | Li₂Mn₂/₃Nb₁/₃O₂F, up to 1000 Wh/kg, Fig. 9a |
| [37] | Yabuuchi et al., *PNAS* 2015 | Li₁.₃Nb₀.₃Mn₀.₄O₂, Fig. 9b |
| [38] | Nakajima & Yabuuchi, *Chem. Mater.* 2017 | Li₁.₂₅Nb₀.₂₅V₀.₅O₂, Fig. 9c |
| [39] | Lee et al., *Energy Environ. Sci.* 2015 | Li₁.₂Ni₁/₃Ti₁/₃Mo₂/₁₅O₂, Fig. 9d |
| [40] | Obrovac, Mao, Dahn, *Solid State Ionics* 1998 | DRX without d⁰ cations (ball-milled LiFeO₂, LiTiO₂) |
| [41] | Chen, Ahn, Chen, *ACS Energy Lett.* 2021 | Short-range cation ordering |
| [42] | Lee et al., *Nat. Commun.* 2017 | Partial fluorine substitution |
| [43] | Zhang et al., *ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces* 2021 | Incorporating F⁻ while avoiding LiF impurities |
| [44] | Abdellahi et al., *Chem. Mater.* 2016 | Sloping voltage profiles from cation disorder |

The same section also cites two references that are not about DRX:
- [27] Manthiram, *Nat. Commun.* 2020, for the general belief that Li/transition-metal ordering is needed (aenm-2022, p. 9; listed p. 14).
- [11] VESTA software, for the crystal-structure drawing in Fig. 8a (aenm-2022, p. 10).

None of the other reviews cites DRX literature:
- The 2021 *Energy Storage Materials* coatings review only mentions "disordered rock salt type" cathodes once in its conclusions, with no citation (ensm-2021, p. 16).
- The *Materials Today* recycling review (mattod-2020) and the 2020 *Energy Storage Materials* perspective (ensm-2020) do not discuss DRX cathodes.
